particulars: All names, dates, places, store names, dollar amounts, heights, weights, print point counts, sentence length, statutes and agency names are absent.

items.record: The case is a criminal armed-robbery prosecution of one man: "charged him with two counts of armed robbery"
items.reading: Primary guess is a child-welfare or family-court file narrating a family's conduct, with a records-driven prosecution only as an alternative
items.loss: The basic setting and type of proceeding is misidentified.

items.record: The wrongful conviction rested on cross-racial eyewitness picks made on a second look and based on the eyes, despite mismatched descriptions: "I think it was him... It's his eyes. 80 percent."
items.reading: absent; the false account is pictured as an archival document or system output
items.loss: This is the actual evidentiary mechanism that produced the false finding.

items.record: A forensic examiner's report claimed a statewide database search that never happened: "they were loaded but never searched, although his report said they had been"
items.reading: Manufacture is described generically as selective records, faulty software or back-filling
items.loss: This is the specific way the official record misstated what had been done.

items.record: The examiner discarded a usable print, and testimony that cleaning removes prints was later shown to be wrong: "the print from the gum wrapper, which Babb called of no value, did have value and appeared to be a whorl"
items.loss: Exculpatory evidence was suppressed through expert judgment and unsupported testimony.

items.record: A witness who knew the defendant said police steered her and insisted it was not him: "an officer pointed to Brown's photo and asked whether she was sure it wasn't him"
items.loss: Police influence on identification and an ignored insider witness are missing.

items.record: The jury split: it acquitted on one count and convicted on the other only after a judge urged unanimity: "Judge Henry Hight gave an Allen charge"
items.loss: The record shows a contested, pressured verdict rather than a smooth official story.

items.record: The defence lawyer failed to show the defendant didn't fit the descriptions: "photo... showing a full beard and a thin face" and "5 feet 9 inches and 150 pounds"
items.loss: Weak defence representation was a cause of the conviction.

items.record: Trial exhibits were destroyed, and courts excused it for lack of bad faith: "no proof the clerk had acted in bad faith"
items.reading: Claims the archive that preserved the false account also preserves evidence of how it was made
items.loss: The reading gets the evidence dynamic backwards: physical evidence was lost and the institution was excused.

items.record: Exoneration came from rerunning preserved prints, which pointed to another identified man: "one of the three prints came from a man identified as Daris J."
items.loss: The concrete turning point was an alternative perpetrator found by database search.

items.record: An innocence organisation fought through a long chain of failed appeals and motions, and an internal review of the examiner was forced into disclosure: "The court ordered the review disclosed"
items.reading: An unspecified counter-force at a threshold
items.loss: The record contains the sequence and actors of the challenge, including the setbacks.

items.record: The case ended fully: the state consented to a new trial and then dropped the charge, while defending trial counsel: "the state dismissed the charge against Brown"
items.reading: Places the case still at a threshold, with slow partial vindication or a stall
items.loss: The resolution and how far along the case is are both misstated.

items.record: The harm fell on one working man and on his custody of his son, and he served years before release: "I had a full-time job and custody of my son"
items.reading: Diffuse harm to families or communities, possibly many
items.loss: The scale and the individual nature of the harm are misdescribed.
